## Target context
- Repo: DontPanic
- Env: dev
- Project: (none)
- Command: 1 (see structured target_context.commands_run)

[F001] $ PYTHONPATH=scripts python -m pytest scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/tests/test_f001_agent_brief.py -q

All 13 targeted tests pass. The F001 `agent_brief` module is fully implemented at `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/agent_brief.py` and renders a deterministic operating brief from live source-of-truth data: supported commands come from `agent_manifest.bootstrap_manifest().supported_commands` (so `agent`/`orchestrate` will appear automatically once F002 adds them), worker executors from `executors.AGENT_REGISTRY` (sorted, no invented labels), runtime version from `dontpanic_orchestrate.__version__`, and config-home status from `global_config`. The brief renders all seven acceptance items — the operator-vs-worker distinction, the verbatim "not Kubernetes, Airflow, or IT orchestration" warning, the canonical `projects add -> plan lock -> orchestrate/dispatch-from-plan -> ... -> approve/resume/close` workflow, and a `GENERATOR_VERSION` plus SHA-256 `content_hash` over the rendered body for F003's managed-block staleness detection. The test suite proves source-tracking by mutating fabricated `BriefInputs` (added `orchestrate`/`agent` commands and a `gemini-builder` executor) and asserting the rendered text and content hash change accordingly, with all tests isolating `$DONTPANIC_HOME` to `tmp_path` so the real home is never touched. No code changes were needed — the existing implementation and tests were already correct and green.
